title: Observation
description: What the extractor believes one source says (housamkak v3 §6.2, §13.1) — one line of llm-wiki/states/observations/<source_id>.jsonl. A noisy semantic measurement, never truth, so it is fully attributed: source, verbatim evidence span, extractor and prompt version, confidence. The extractor writes the record without observation_id and extracted_at; apply mints both (observation_id = obs_ + 12 hex of sha256(source_id · claim_key · stance · evidence_span), plus the override when present), so re-extracting an unchanged source reproduces the same ids and apply is a no-op. A human files the same record with extractor.model human:<name>; only such a record may carry override. Under extract-v2 the record may carry decay_profile, and every relationships[].predicate is one of the twelve canonical predicates — enforced on extract-v2 and manual records; extract-v1 rows stay valid as written and map to the canonical set at view build.

model.description: The model id that extracted, or human:<name> for a hand-written observation.

prompt_version.description: The extraction contract the record was written under — extract-v2 today (extract-v1 rows stay valid); manual for humans.

claim_key.description: Dotted lowercase path naming the question the claim answers, most general segment first: <domain>.<subject>.<aspect>, 2–5 segments. Exact-match joins evidence across sources.

stance.description: §13.1 vocabulary — how this observation bears on the claim its key names.

confidence.description: The extractor's semantic confidence that the source really says this, 0–1.

evidence_span.description: Verbatim text from the archive. validate checks it appears there, whitespace-normalized.

type.description: The wiki's page types — an entity of this type renders under the matching shelf.

subject.description: An entity name listed in entities.

predicate.description: One of the twelve canonical predicates on extract-v2 and manual records; extract-v1 rows may carry any word, mapped to the canonical set at view build.

object.description: An entity name listed in entities.

conditions.description: When the claim holds — scope, audience, time. Two claims under one key with disjoint conditions are siblings, not contradictions.

decay_profile.description: §8.8 — the extractor's judgment of how fast this claim ages. Optional: the engine derives the channel default when absent, and the newest explicit profile among a claim's supporting observations wins.

privacy.description: The note's vocabulary. The layer is fully tracked: the shared segment accepts only public and internal, the private segment also accepts private, and secret is refused in both.

run_id.description: The run that appended this row (spec.md `### Ledger rows`) — run_ + 12 hex of sha256(actor · verb · timestamp · the input hashes · views_before), the same id stamped on the row's states/audit_log.jsonl entry. Optional: absent on every row from Phases 1–5, present on every row Phase 6 on appends.

override.description: Human review (§12.6): set a claim's status directly. Valid only on a human:<name> record; lands as a human_override transition.
